scenes.say: Ever wondered how big companies keep all their logins and permissions in sync? Let's break down Active Directory.

scenes.label: Directory
scenes.sub: Active Directory stores users, computers, and groups for the whole network.
scenes.say: Active Directory is like a giant address book for your network. It tracks users, computers, and groups all in one place.
Domain controllers are special servers. They handle authentication, store the directory, and sync updates with each other. Regular servers can't do any of that.

scenes.title: User & Group Tasks
scenes.say: You can easily find locked accounts, unlock users, and list group members using PowerShell commands.

scenes.question: How many domain controllers per domain?
scenes.right: Always run at least two for redundancy.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: running only one domain controller. Always use at least two so you don't lose authentication if one goes down.
